title: Characteristic and mantissa
summary: Split log N into a whole part (the power of 10) and a decimal part (the digits).
alt: A number line from -4 to 5 with log N marked, split into a characteristic and a mantissa.

ch.label: Characteristic
ch.text: The whole-number part of the log.

ma.label: Mantissa
ma.text: The decimal part of the log.

shapes.text: Mantissa {{lm|=3}} depends only on the digits
{{if pw<0 | Negative characteristic: write it with a bar | Characteristic = digits before the point minus 1}}

steps.title: A number in standard form
steps.narration: Write the number as \( m \times 10^e \) with \( 1 \le m < 10 \). Here \( N = {{m|1}} \times 10^{ {{pw|int}} } = {{N|6}} \).

steps.title: Where is its logarithm?
steps.narration: \( \log N = \log m + e \). The point sits between **{{pw|int}}** and **{{pw+1|int}}** on the number line.

steps.title: Characteristic
steps.narration: The whole-number part is the [[ch|characteristic]]. It is just the power of 10: **{{pw|int}}**.

steps.title: Mantissa
steps.narration: The decimal part is the [[ma|mantissa]]: \( \log {{m|1}} = {{lm|=3}} \). It is always between 0 and 1.

steps.title: Move the decimal point
steps.narration: Now \( N = {{4.5*10^(-2)|3}} \). The digits are the same, so the **mantissa is the same**; only the characteristic changes to **−2**.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.narration: Change the digits **m** and the power **e**. Watch which part moves.

formulas.title: Standard form
formulas.text: Move the decimal point until one non-zero digit is before it.

formulas.title: Split the log
formulas.text: e is the characteristic and log m is the mantissa.

challenges.title: Same digits, same mantissa
challenges.hint: Both numbers have the digits 4 and 5.
challenges.explain: Same digits mean the same mantissa. Only the characteristic changes (1 and 3).

challenges.title: Mantissa
challenges.prompt: Set the digits to 3.2. What is the mantissa, \( \log 3.2 \)? (3 decimal places)
challenges.hint: Use the value shown in the picture or a calculator.

intro: Every common logarithm has two parts. One tells the size, the other tells the digits.
takeaways: Characteristic = the power of 10 (a whole number).
Mantissa = log of the digits (between 0 and 1).
Moving the decimal point changes only the characteristic.

notes.title: Bar notation
notes.text: For N < 1 the characteristic is negative but the mantissa stays positive, so we write the minus sign as a bar over the number.
